deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is the title leaf of a bundle of natural-philosophical fragments. The title, page and bundle labels, and section index suggest it is a later editorial copy or arrangement, probably prepared for the posthumous edition. The handwriting looks like a copyist's, not Riemann's own hand; this is an inference from the title 'Naturphilosophische Aphorismen von B. Riemann' and the editorial references to page numbers.

Contents:

(a) The 'Englisches Blatt 1' is Riemann's verbatim English quotation of Newton's third letter to Bentley (25 Feb 1692/3). It is the passage holding that unmediated action at a distance through a vacuum is an absurdity no competent philosopher could accept. It motivates Riemann's programme of replacing action at a distance by propagation through a medium, i.e. 'Gravitation und Licht'.

(b) An editorial index of the bundle:
- 1–21 Höhere Mechanik
- 22–31 Psychologisch
- 31–36 Höhere Mechanik / gravitation (struck through, partly illegible)
- 36–38 Zweckmässigkeit der organischen [Wesen?]
- 38–40 Principien der Naturerklärung (Blatt 16 und 17)

There is also a pencil list 'Psychologisches u. Naturphilosophisches 1.–4.' with page references.

(c) 'Causalität' (Blatt 2), three theses:
- I. What an agent strives to effect must be determined by the concept of the agent; its action depends only on its own essence.
- II. This requirement is met if the agent strives to preserve or restore itself.
- III. Such action is conceivable only if the agent is a state or relation, not a thing or being. Striving to preserve or restore something presupposes possible deviations of varying degree, so that when other strivings conflict the target is only approximately maintained. But there are no degrees of being; gradation is conceivable only for states or relations. Hence a self-preserving agent must be a state or relation.

(d) A pencil addendum, 'Einfachste Art des Wirkens', restricts these theses to the case where action is ascribed to a simple real ground (Realgrund). When two things a and b are brought into connection by an external cause, a consequence c may attach either to the connectedness itself or to the change of its degree. The simplest assumption is that c attaches to the connectedness. A struck clause adds that c then ceases when the connection ceases.

My interpretive gloss: this is the metaphysical basis for Riemann's later view of forces as tendencies of a medium (a state) to restore itself, which underlies his ether and 'Geistesmassen' speculations. There is nothing to compute.

results.what: Quotation of Newton's third letter to Bentley rejecting unmediated action at a distance
results.modern_name: Newton's rejection of action at a distance (Bentley correspondence)

results.what: Causality theses: an agent's action is determined by its concept; it strives for self-preservation or restoration; so the agent must be a state or relation, admitting degrees
results.modern_name: Riemann's natural-philosophical fragments on causality (Herbartian-influenced metaphysics)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann; material of this kind appears in the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' of the Gesammelte Werke (Weber/Dedekind, 1876/1892)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a philosophical title or index page with a Newton quotation and causality aphorisms. It belongs to Riemann's known philosophical fragments, which were largely edited in his Gesammelte Werke. It contains no mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The page appears to be in a copyist's or editor's hand (a fair copy titled 'Naturphilosophische Aphorismen von B. Riemann'), not Riemann's autograph; the pencil index and page references are editorial.
The bracket after '(Englisches Blatt 1.)' reads roughly '[Erste Anmerkung zu S. 12?]'; the reading is uncertain, and the transcription's '(Anm. Anmerkung ...)' doubles the word.
In the index, '31–36' is preceded by a struck word, and the heading 'Höhere Mechanik' in '1.–21.' is also heavily inked or struck; the parenthetical after 31–36 is likely '(Gravitat.)' but uncertain.
The 36–38 entry appears to continue 'Zweckmässigkeit der organischen [Wesen]'; the final word is cut off at the margin.

The first pencil addendum breaks off mid-sentence ('und zwar kann diese Folge c') and the second at 'eine Folge c geknüpft sein, welche'. These are genuine incomplete sentences, not transcription losses.
